title: Are carbs bad for weight loss?
desc: No. Carbohydrate is not automatically fattening. Overall energy intake, food quality and portions matter.

title: Is fat bad for weight loss?
desc: No. Dietary fat is essential but energy dense, so portions and the wider diet matter.

title: Does sleep affect weight?
desc: Yes. Sleep can influence appetite, food choices, energy, mood and activity.

title: Do I need a gym to lose weight?
desc: No. Walking, home exercise, sport, cycling and ordinary daily movement can all contribute.

title: Should men count calories?
desc: Calorie tracking can be useful for some men, but it is not compulsory.

title: Is Shift Some Timber a replacement for my GP?
desc: No. It is not a replacement for NHS primary care, emergency services or individual medical assessment.

title: How often should I weigh myself?
desc: There is no single right frequency. The useful part is looking at the trend rather than reacting to one reading.

title: What is the 20% Club?
desc: A milestone some people use to describe losing 20% of their starting body weight. It is not a universal target.

title: What is a healthy waist-to-height ratio?
desc: NHS guidance uses the simple message of trying to keep your waist below half your height.

title: Why do men get belly fat?
desc: Men commonly store a greater proportion of fat centrally. Genetics, age, hormones, energy balance, activity, sleep and alcohol can all contribute.

title: Is 20% weight loss realistic for everyone?
desc: No. A 20% reduction is a major milestone, not a universal target. A practical, plain-English guide for UK men.

title: Can I have a BBQ while losing weight?
desc: Absolutely. A barbecue can fit into a healthy week. A practical, plain-English guide for UK men.

title: Why do my knees hurt more after gaining weight?
desc: Greater body mass can increase load through weight-bearing joints, but knee pain can have several causes.

title: Is Wegovy the same as Ozempic?
desc: They both contain semaglutide, but they are distinct branded products with different licensed uses and dosing pathways.

title: How quickly should a man lose weight?
desc: There is no single perfect weekly rate for every man. A sustainable rate depends on starting weight, health, food intake, activity and treatment.

title: How much protein do men need?
desc: Protein needs vary with body size, age, health, activity and goals. A calculator is only a planning estimate.

title: Can men take Mounjaro?
desc: Yes, men can be prescribed tirzepatide (Mounjaro) when it is clinically appropriate and they meet the relevant prescribing criteria.

title: Does losing weight raise testosterone?
desc: Weight loss may improve testosterone levels in some men living with obesity, but symptoms alone cannot diagnose testosterone deficiency.

title: Can walking help weight loss?
desc: Yes. Walking increases activity and energy expenditure and can be a sustainable part of weight management.

title: Can women use the public tools?
desc: The public calculators are general information tools, although the brand voice is designed around adult men.

title: Is the Health MOT a medical assessment?
desc: No. It is an informational self-check and does not diagnose a condition or establish treatment eligibility.

title: Can weight loss lower blood pressure?
desc: For many people carrying excess weight, weight loss can contribute to lower blood pressure alongside other measures.

title: Is BMI accurate for men?
desc: BMI is a useful screening measure, but it does not distinguish muscle from fat and does not directly show where body fat is stored.

title: Do I need breakfast to lose weight?
desc: No. The best eating pattern is one that supports good nutrition and can be maintained.

title: Does alcohol cause belly fat?
desc: Alcohol provides calories and can influence appetite, food choices and sleep.

title: Why does my weight change day to day?
desc: Water, salt, carbohydrate intake, bowel contents, exercise, alcohol and timing can all move scale weight.

title: Can I exercise on GLP-1 treatment?
desc: Many people can remain active, but exercise should match health, fitness and treatment effects.

title: Does belly fat increase health risk?
desc: Higher levels of central or visceral fat are associated with increased cardiometabolic risk.

title: Does Shift Some Timber prescribe medication yet?
desc: No. Shift Some Timber does not prescribe or supply medication. A practical, plain-English guide for UK men.

title: Can weight affect sleep apnoea?
desc: Yes. Excess weight is an important risk factor for obstructive sleep apnoea, although it is not the only cause.

title: Can losing weight reduce diabetes risk?
desc: For people at increased risk of type 2 diabetes, weight loss and lifestyle change can reduce risk.

title: What is a Founding Shifter?
desc: Someone who joins Shift and wants useful updates. A practical, plain-English guide for UK men.

title: Will GLP-1 treatment make me lose muscle?
desc: Weight loss can include some lean tissue. Adequate nutrition and resistance exercise can help support muscle and strength.

title: Will my Health MOT data be saved?
desc: Public Health MOT answers are not saved to a member health history unless you use an account-backed feature that clearly tells you it will save them.

title: Is GLP-1 treatment only for women?
desc: No. GLP-1 and related prescription weight-management medicines are not women's treatments.

title: Can stress make me gain weight?
desc: Stress can contribute indirectly by affecting eating, alcohol, sleep and activity.

title: Can men take Wegovy?
desc: Yes. Wegovy (semaglutide) can be prescribed to eligible adult men following appropriate clinical assessment.

title: Can I eat takeaways and still lose weight?
desc: Yes. Takeaways can fit into a weight-management plan depending on frequency, portions, sides and drinks.

title: What is a weight-loss plateau?
desc: A plateau is a period when body weight changes very little despite continued efforts.

title: Can weight loss improve cholesterol?
desc: Weight management, diet and activity can improve parts of the lipid profile for some people.

title: What is The Timber Mill?
desc: The Shift Some Timber shop for clothing, useful gear, guides and future member rewards.

title: What happens if I stop GLP-1 treatment?
desc: Appetite and weight may change after stopping treatment, so maintenance planning and follow-up matter.

title: Can I drink alcohol on GLP-1 medication?
desc: There is no one answer for everybody. Alcohol may worsen dehydration or gastrointestinal symptoms for some people, so discuss your situation with your prescriber.

title: Is Mounjaro the same as Ozempic?
desc: No. Mounjaro contains tirzepatide; Ozempic contains semaglutide. A practical, plain-English guide for UK men.
